commands.review_summary:
The PR replaces five memory-core dreaming snippet `.slice(0, N)` truncations with `truncateUtf16Safe` via the memory-core SDK facade and adds a surrogate-boundary integration test.

PR surface: Source +7, Tests +186. Total +193 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Source inspection gives a high-confidence reproduction path: current main uses raw `.slice(0, 280)` on dreaming snippets, and a surrogate pair straddling that code-unit boundary can produce a lone surrogate; I did not run a live current-main repro in this read-only review.

target.title: [AI] fix(memory): use truncateUtf16Safe for dreaming snippet truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where dreaming snippet truncation in `memory-core` can produce invalid UTF-16 output. When a complex emoji or surrogate pair straddles the 280-character truncation boundary, `.slice(0, 280)` cuts between the high and low surrogate code units, producing a lone surrogate that can cause display corruption, JSON encoding failures, or database rejections downstream.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace all 5 `.slice(0, N)` calls in `extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-phases.ts` with `truncateUtf16Safe` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-engine-foundation` (the standard SDK facade, already used by `manager-search.ts` in the same extension). `truncateUtf16Safe` checks whether the cut position falls inside a surrogate pair (high surrogate `0xD800–0xDBFF` followed by low surrogate `0xDC00–0xDFFF`) and drops the orphaned high surrogate. The change is +6/-5 in a single file.

## User Impact

None for typical text content. For memory content that happens to contain an emoji or complex Unicode character at the truncation boundary, the dreaming snippet no longer includes a lone surrogate character, preventing potential downstream encoding issues.

## Evidence

**Environment**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.13.1, OpenClaw 2026.6.11, commit `9ae8803b90`.

### 1. Lone surrogate reproduction at the 280-char boundary

Both `DAILY_INGESTION_MAX_SNIPPET_CHARS` and `SESSION_INGESTION_MAX_SNIPPET_CHARS` are `280` (`dreaming-phases.ts:99,109`). With emoji at position 279–280:

```
$ node --import tsx -e "
import { truncateUtf16Safe } from '@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice';
const text = 'A'.repeat(279) + '😀';
console.log('.slice(0, 280):     last code unit 0x' +
  text.slice(0, 280).charCodeAt(279).toString(16) + ' (LONE HIGH SURROGATE)');
console.log('truncateUtf16Safe:   ' +
  truncateUtf16Safe(text, 280).length + ' code units (clean)');
"
.slice(0, 280):     last code unit 0xD83D (LONE HIGH SURROGATE)
truncateUtf16Safe:   279 code units (clean)
```

### 2. Real dreaming ingestion proof — emoji in daily notes + session corpus

A full dreaming sweep was run against the patched branch with emoji-rich content at the truncation boundary:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/surrogate-proof.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

The test:

1. Creates a workspace with a daily note containing emoji at the 280-char boundary
2. Creates a session transcript with emoji in both near-boundary and overflow positions
3. Runs `runDreamingSweepPhases` (the full dreaming ingestion pipeline)
4. Performs code-unit-level verification that the daily markdown output, session corpus output, and all log messages contain zero lone surrogates

### 3. Existing unit test coverage

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-phases.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  50 passed (50)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
```

### 4. Import boundary (fixes Codex review finding)

Import path updated from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` → `openclaw/plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-engine-foundation`, matching the existing SDK facade used by `manager-search.ts` in the same extension.

### What was NOT tested

Full dreaming ingestion sweep with real memory files containing emoji at the truncation boundary from a live production workspace. Covered by: 50 dreaming-phase unit tests, 18 utf16-slice tests, plus the new surrogate-proof integration test.

**Proof test file**: `extensions/memory-core/src/surrogate-proof.test.ts`
